parts.title: Vol 9 Test Passage 3
parts.passageHtml:
The mystery of Easter Island What could possibly explain the lack of vegetation on Easter Island?

The giant stone statues of Easter Island in the Pacific Ocean have perplexed archaeologists ever since European explorers first witnessed them three centuries ago. Jacob Roggeveen, the Dutch seaman who gave the island its name in 1722, was amazed by the statues, each of which clearly weighed several tonnes. But as there were no forests on the island, he could not comprehend how people devoid of heavy timber could build and erect something that size. It was also remarkable considering the absence of metal objects for carving and cutting, and the reliance on mere human strength as no draught animals could be seen either. Roggeveen was equally amazed as to how the islanders could have come to colonise such a remote place. Their canoes were leaky and frail, not the sort of ocean-going craft that could survive a three-week sea journey. At the time of his visit, it seemed evident the islanders were living in extremely poor conditions and that there was no cultivation of crops.

What was the mystery behind the statues? In the 1970s, the author Erich von Däniken suggested the statues were the work of extraterrestrial beings. It was hard to believe the stones were the work of humans who were more than 2,000 miles from the nearest mainland, so for a short period of time his theory appealed to those fascinated with space travel. But for serious academics, the puzzle of the statues has caused a deep divide. Some archaeologists see Easter Island as an example of what can happen when the lust for material splendour - ever bigger stone carvings in this case is satisfied at the expense of the environment. Others, meanwhile, take a different view. The island, these scholars argue, suffered at the hands of introduced diseases, notably smallpox, and a slave trade that stole a huge proportion of its indigenous population. At the heart of the debate is the issue of the island's deforestation. There is no doubt that the island was once covered in palm trees. There is also no doubt that something happened that caused the island to become completely denuded over a short period of time. But was it the islanders who triggered this environmental degradation or another event beyond their control, such as the introduction of rats? It is an indisputable fact that rats found their way to the island, although exactly how is a matter of debate.

In 2005, the anthropologist Jared Diamond claimed the islanders started building ceremonial statues in an atmosphere of rivalry between the many clans. To move the statues from the island's quarry in the south-east, they needed to cut large logs for the construction of long 'canoe ladders' to carry them to the coast. For its transport alone, each statue would have required several trees to be cut down. As a result of the deforestation, Diamond believes food production fell dramatically. Consequently the population collapsed from perhaps as many as 15,000 to the few thousand that were eking out a living by the time Roggeveen arrived. Smallpox and slavery killed off those who remained, but the islanders were on the way to total collapse even without any European contact, says Diamond.

But not everyone is convinced. Professor Terry Hunt, an anthropologist at the University of Hawaii, says: 'There is no evidence that a population collapse occurred before European contact.' He is supported by Professor Carl Lipo of California State University. They argue that Easter Island was colonised by the first Polynesian seafarers nowhere near as early as supposed. They say the first people to arrive came around AD1200, about 400 years later than other scientists have suggested from radio-carbon dating. This makes it implausible for the population to have reached the 15,000 figure that would have caused such a fast ecocide. They also believe the deforestation occurred over a longer period as a result of climate change, and rats probably also played a part. The islanders did not go through a population collapse until after the arrival of Europeans, they say.

Hunt has examined new data from the Hawaiian and other Pacific islands that shows that by early historic times the deforestation of Easter Island was already complete, or nearly so. A dense forest of palm trees and shrubs had mostly disappeared and as a result, as many as six land bird species had also become extinct. Crucially, much of the forest damage appears to have been done before evidence of fires on the island. However, almost all of the palm seed shells discovered on the island were found to have been gnawed by rats which would have made them unable to germinate. Evidence from other Pacific islands also confirms how destructive rats can be. However, John Flenley of New Zealand's Massey University, who carried out much of the radio-carbon work on Easter Island, says there is ample evidence for a much earlier arrival of Polynesian settlers. He refutes the arguments of the sceptics: whilst admitting that the Europeans did bring certain disasters, he maintains that Hunt and Lipo are ignoring archaeological, botanical and sedimentological evidence proving the island was transformed from a subtropical rainforest to a treeless landscape. The radio-carbon dating points to an initial colonisation before AD900, Flenley argues. This was ample time for the rapid deforestation, environmental collapse and a population crash, he insists.

Why all this is important today is not, of course, lost in the age of globalisation, climate change and a rapidly growing world population in the billions. As Diamond says: 'The parallels between Easter Island and the whole of the modern world are chillingly obvious.'

questions.text: When Dutchman Jacob Roggeveen sailed to Easter Island in 1722, he was amazed by the stone statues he saw for a number of reasons. Firstly, it was clear that they were immensely heavy, and there was no 27__________ around, which would have helped with their construction. Roggeveen did not think the inhabitants had any metal tools, or animals for heavy labour either. Another mystery was the poor quality of the local inhabitants' 28__________; Roggeveen wondered how the people had managed to survive long trips. At the time of Roggeveen's visit, he observed that the people were living in 29__________ and there was no evidence of successful 30__________ on the island.
questions.explanationHtml:
27. D

Câu hỏi: Firstly, it was clear that they were immensely heavy, and there was no ____ around, which would have helped with their construction.

(Trước tiên, rõ ràng chúng cực kỳ nặng và không có ______ xung quanh, thứ có thể giúp xây dựng chúng.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

But as there were no forests on the island, he could not comprehend how people devoid of heavy timber could build and erect something that size.

(Nhưng vì trên đảo không có rừng, ông không thể hiểu nổi làm thế nào những người thiếu thốn gỗ lớn lại có thể xây và dựng lên một công trình lớn như vậy.)

=> Đáp án: D. wood = forests

questions.text: When Dutchman Jacob Roggeveen sailed to Easter Island in 1722, he was amazed by the stone statues he saw for a number of reasons. Firstly, it was clear that they were immensely heavy, and there was no 27__________ around, which would have helped with their construction. Roggeveen did not think the inhabitants had any metal tools, or animals for heavy labour either. Another mystery was the poor quality of the local inhabitants' 28__________; Roggeveen wondered how the people had managed to survive long trips. At the time of Roggeveen's visit, he observed that the people were living in 29__________ and there was no evidence of successful 30__________ on the island.
questions.explanationHtml:
28. C

Câu hỏi: Another mystery was the poor quality of the local inhabitants'______

(Một bí ẩn khác là chất lượng kém của ______ của người dân địa phương)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

Their canoes were leaky and frail, not the sort of ocean-going craft that could survive a three-week sea journey.

(Những chiếc xuồng của họ rò rỉ và ọp ẹp, không phải loại thuyền có thể chịu được một chuyến đi biển kéo dài ba tuần.)

=> Đáp án: C. boats = canoes

questions.text: When Dutchman Jacob Roggeveen sailed to Easter Island in 1722, he was amazed by the stone statues he saw for a number of reasons. Firstly, it was clear that they were immensely heavy, and there was no 27__________ around, which would have helped with their construction. Roggeveen did not think the inhabitants had any metal tools, or animals for heavy labour either. Another mystery was the poor quality of the local inhabitants' 28__________; Roggeveen wondered how the people had managed to survive long trips. At the time of Roggeveen's visit, he observed that the people were living in 29__________ and there was no evidence of successful 30__________ on the island.
questions.explanationHtml:
29. A

Câu hỏi: At the time of Roggeveen's visit, he observed that the people were living in______

(Vào thời điểm Roggeveen đến thăm, ông nhận thấy người dân sống trong______)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

At the time of his visit, it seemed evident the islanders were living in extremely poor conditions and that there was no cultivation of crops.

(Vào thời điểm ông đến thăm, rõ ràng là người dân trên đảo đang sống trong điều kiện vô cùng nghèo khó và không có hoạt động trồng trọt.)

Giải thích: poor conditions = poverty.

=> Đáp án: A. poverty

questions.text: When Dutchman Jacob Roggeveen sailed to Easter Island in 1722, he was amazed by the stone statues he saw for a number of reasons. Firstly, it was clear that they were immensely heavy, and there was no 27__________ around, which would have helped with their construction. Roggeveen did not think the inhabitants had any metal tools, or animals for heavy labour either. Another mystery was the poor quality of the local inhabitants' 28__________; Roggeveen wondered how the people had managed to survive long trips. At the time of Roggeveen's visit, he observed that the people were living in 29__________ and there was no evidence of successful 30__________ on the island.
questions.explanationHtml:
30. B

Câu hỏi: and there was no evidence of successful ______on the island.

(và không có bằng chứng về ______ thành công trên đảo.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

At the time of his visit, it seemed evident the islanders were living in extremely poor conditions and that there was no cultivation of crops.

(Vào thời điểm ông đến thăm, rõ ràng là người dân trên đảo đang sống trong điều kiện vô cùng nghèo khó và không có hoạt động trồng trọt.)

=> Đáp án: B. agriculture = cultivation of crops

questions.text: 31 Erich von Däniken's claims were briefly accepted by some sections of society.
questions.explanationHtml:
31. NO

Câu hỏi: Erich von Däniken's claims were briefly accepted by some sections of society.

(Các tuyên bố của Erich von Däniken đã được nhiều tầng lớp xã hội chấp nhận trong thời gian ngắn.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

It was hard to believe the stones were the work of humans who were more than 2,000 miles from the nearest mainland, so for a short period of time his theory appealed to those fascinated with space travel.

(Khó tin rằng những tảng đá đó là tác phẩm của con người khi họ ở cách đất liền gần nhất hơn 2.000 dặm, vì vậy trong một thời gian ngắn, lý thuyết của ông đã thu hút những người say mê du hành vũ trụ. )

Giải thích: Câu hỏi đề cập đến “some sections of society” nhưng bài đọc chỉ có “those fascinated with space travel”.

questions.text: 32 Archaeologists removed valuable artefacts from the island.
questions.explanationHtml:
32. NG

Câu hỏi: Archaeologists removed valuable artefacts from the island.

(Các nhà khảo cổ đã lấy đi những hiện vật có giá trị khỏi hòn đảo.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

Some archaeologists see Easter Island as an example of what can happen when the lust for material splendour - ever bigger stone carvings in this case is satisfied at the expense of the environment.

(Một số nhà khảo cổ học xem đảo Phục Sinh là một ví dụ về những gì có thể xảy ra khi lòng tham vật chất - trong trường hợp này là những tác phẩm điêu khắc đá ngày càng lớn - được thỏa mãn bằng cách hủy hoại môi trường.)

Giải thích: Bài đọc không nhắc đến việc các nhà khảo cổ lấy hiện vật khỏi đảo, chỉ nói rằng một số nhà khảo cổ có quan điểm rằng người dân trên đảo đã phá hủy môi trường vì họ quá tập trung xây tượng đá lớn.

questions.text: 33 Smallpox continued to affect Easter Island's inhabitants for centuries.
questions.explanationHtml:
33. NG

Câu hỏi: Smallpox continued to affect Easter Island's inhabitants for centuries.

(Bệnh đậu mùa tiếp tục ảnh hưởng đến cư dân đảo Phục Sinh suốt nhiều thế kỷ.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

The island, these scholars argue, suffered at the hands of introduced diseases, notably smallpox,

(Theo các học giả này, hòn đảo đã phải hứng chịu sự tàn phá của các bệnh dịch du nhập, đặc biệt là bệnh đậu mùa.)

Giải thích: Bài chỉ nói bệnh đậu mùa ảnh hưởng đến dân đảo, không nói kéo dài hàng thế kỷ.

questions.text: 34 It remains open to question whether Easter Island was once covered in forest.
questions.explanationHtml:
34. NO

Câu hỏi: It remains open to question whether Easter Island was once covered in forest.

(Việc đảo Phục Sinh từng được bao phủ bởi rừng vẫn còn là điều gây tranh cãi.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

There is no doubt that the island was once covered in palm trees.

(Không còn nghi ngờ gì nữa, hòn đảo này trước đây từng được bao phủ bởi những hàng cây cọ.)

Giải thích: Câu hỏi nói “vẫn còn tranh cãi”, nhưng bài nói “không còn nghi ngờ”.

questions.text: 35 The way that rats arrived on Easter Island is still to be established.
questions.explanationHtml:
35. YES

Câu hỏi: The way that rats arrived on Easter Island is still to be established.

(Cách mà chuột đến đảo Phục Sinh vẫn chưa được xác định rõ.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

It is an indisputable fact that rats found their way to the island, although exactly how is a matter of debate

(Không thể phủ nhận rằng chuột đã tìm đường đến hòn đảo này, mặc dù cách thức chính xác vẫn còn là vấn đề gây tranh cãi.)

Giải thích: “still to be established” = vẫn chưa xác định rõ.

questions.text: 36 What does Jared Diamond blame for the lack of vegetation on Easter Island?
questions.explanationHtml:
36. C

Câu hỏi: What does Jared Diamond blame for the lack of vegetation on Easter Island? A. The construction of stone statues B. Climate change over a long period C. A method of transportation D. The arrival of Europeans

(Jared Diamond cho rằng điều gì gây ra sự thiếu thảm thực vật trên đảo Phục Sinh? A. Việc xây dựng các bức tượng đá B. Biến đổi khí hậu trong thời gian dài C. Một phương thức vận chuyển D. Sự xuất hiện của người châu Âu)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

To move the statues from the island's quarry in the south-east, they needed to cut large logs for the construction of long 'canoe ladders' to carry them to the coast. For its transport alone, each statue would have required several trees to be cut down.

(Để di chuyển các bức tượng từ mỏ đá ở phía đông nam của hòn đảo, họ cần phải chặt những khúc gỗ lớn để làm những chiếc "thang thuyền" dài để vận chuyển chúng ra bờ biển. Chỉ riêng việc vận chuyển, mỗi bức tượng đã cần phải đốn hạ vài cây.)

questions.text: 37 What do Hunt and Lipo suggest about the population of Easter Island?
questions.explanationHtml:
37. B

Câu hỏi: What do Hunt and Lipo suggest about the population of Easter Island? A. It collapsed before European contact B. The first settlers arrived much later than is widely accepted C. It never exceeded a few thousand inhabitants D. It declined mainly because of disease

(Hunt và Lipo cho rằng điều gì về dân số của đảo Phục Sinh? A. Dân số sụp đổ trước khi người châu Âu đến B. Những người định cư đầu tiên đến muộn hơn nhiều so với quan điểm phổ biến C. Dân số chưa bao giờ vượt quá vài nghìn người D. Dân số suy giảm chủ yếu vì bệnh tật)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

They say the first people to arrive came around AD1200, about 400 years later than other scientists have suggested from radio-carbon dating.

(Họ nói rằng những người đầu tiên đến đây vào khoảng năm 1200 sau Công nguyên, muộn hơn khoảng 400 năm so với những gì các nhà khoa học khác đã đề xuất dựa trên phương pháp định tuổi bằng đồng vị cacbon phóng xạ.)

questions.text: 38 What is suggested about rats on Easter Island in the fifth paragraph?
questions.explanationHtml:
38. A

Câu hỏi: What is suggested about rats on Easter Island in the fifth paragraph? A. They were a likely cause of deforestation B. They arrived after the forests had disappeared C. They had no effect on plant regeneration D. They were introduced by Europeans

(Đoạn văn thứ năm gợi ý điều gì về loài chuột trên đảo Phục Sinh? A. Chúng có thể là nguyên nhân gây nạn phá rừng B. Chúng xuất hiện sau khi rừng biến mất C. Chúng không ảnh hưởng đến sự tái sinh của thực vật D. Chúng được người châu Âu mang đến)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

They also believe the deforestation occurred over a longer period as a result of climate change, and rats probably also played a part.

(Họ cũng tin rằng nạn phá rừng diễn ra trong một thời gian dài do biến đổi khí hậu, và chuột có thể cũng đóng một vai trò trong đó.)

questions.text: 39 Flenley responds to Hunt and Lipo’s theory by
questions.explanationHtml:
39. A

Câu hỏi: Flenley responds to Hunt and Lipo’s theory by A. dismissing it B. partially supporting it C. expanding on their arguments D. avoiding direct criticism

(Flenley phản hồi lý thuyết của Hunt và Lipo bằng cách: A. bác bỏ nó B. phần nào ủng hộ nó C. mở rộng các lập luận của họ D. tránh chỉ trích trực tiếp)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

He refutes the arguments of the sceptics: whilst admitting that the Europeans did bring certain disasters, he maintains that Hunt and Lipo are ignoring archaeological, botanical and sedimentological evidence proving the island was transformed from a subtropical rainforest to a treeless landscape.

(Ông bác bỏ các lập luận của những người hoài nghi: mặc dù thừa nhận rằng người châu Âu thực sự đã mang đến một số thảm họa, ông vẫn cho rằng Hunt và Lipo đang bỏ qua các bằng chứng khảo cổ học, thực vật học và trầm tích học chứng minh rằng hòn đảo đã bị biến đổi từ một khu rừng mưa cận nhiệt đới thành một vùng đất không còn cây cối. )

Giải thích: “refutes” = bác bỏ hoàn toàn.

questions.text: 40 The writer’s purpose in this article is to
questions.explanationHtml:
40. B

Câu hỏi: The writer’s purpose in this article is to A. argue in favour of Diamond’s interpretation B. provide an overview of a series of arguments C. prove that rats were the main cause of deforestation D. criticise modern archaeological methods

(Mục đích của tác giả trong bài viết này là: A. lập luận ủng hộ cách giải thích của Diamond B. cung cấp cái nhìn tổng quan về một loạt lập luận C. chứng minh rằng chuột là nguyên nhân chính gây phá rừng D. chỉ trích các phương pháp khảo cổ học hiện đại)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

Why all this is important today is not, of course, lost in the age of globalisation, climate change and a rapidly growing world population in the billions.

(Tất nhiên, tầm quan trọng của tất cả những điều này ngày nay không hề bị lu mờ trong thời đại toàn cầu hóa, biến đổi khí hậu và dân số thế giới đang tăng nhanh chóng lên hàng tỷ người.)

Giải thích: Bài viết trình bày: nhiều giả thuyết khác nhau, ý kiến của Diamond, Hunt & Lipo, Flenley, vai trò của chuột, bệnh tật, khí hậu…Tác giả không hoàn toàn ủng hộ một bên nào.
